question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x^{2}+y^{2}=4.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$, or equivalently $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1$, in the $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,2 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{4}&=\frac{(2 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{4}+\frac{(2 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{4}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $z\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $2 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.

f(t,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $4x^{2}+y^{2}=64.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $4x^{2}+y^{2}=64$, or equivalently $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{y^{2}}{64}=1$, in the $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨4 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{64}&=\frac{(4 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{16}+\frac{(8 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{64}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨4 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $z\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $4 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $25x^{2}+9z^{2}=225.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $25x^{2}+9z^{2}=225$, or equivalently $\frac{x^{2}}{9}+\frac{z^{2}}{25}=1$, in the $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,z⟩=⟨3 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,5 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{z^2}{25}&=\frac{(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{9}+\frac{(5 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{25}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,y)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨3 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,y,\,5 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

f(t,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $16x^{2}+9y^{2}=576.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $16x^{2}+9y^{2}=576$, or equivalently $\frac{x^{2}}{36}+\frac{y^{2}}{64}=1$, in the $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨6 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{36}+\frac{y^2}{64}&=\frac{(6 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{36}+\frac{(8 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{64}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨6 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $z\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $6 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

$$
f(t,y)=⟨\cos{\left(t \right)},\,y,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,y)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{x^{2}}{1}+\frac{z^{2}}{121}=1.$ What is the third component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{1}+\frac{z^{2}}{121}=1$ in the $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,z⟩=⟨\cos{\left(t \right)},\,11 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{1}+\frac{z^2}{121}&=\frac{(\cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{1}+\frac{(11 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{121}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
f(t,y)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨\cos{\left(t \right)},\,y,\,11 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $11 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.
